name: agy-artifact-prevention
goal: Add a prevention layer for the agy artifact-path failure: custom agent manifest with a tools allowlist that omits the native write tools, --agent selection, and init.tools verification, layered on top of the existing repair-retry fix

nodes.label: Implement prevention (Sonnet)
nodes.prompt:
You are extending a fix in the Tractor repo (this workspace is a git worktree on branch claude/jovial-aryabhata-59c086; work directly here, do NOT commit).

If EVAL_FEEDBACK.md exists in the workspace root, this is a REWORK round: read it first, address every finding, and update WORK_SUMMARY.md. Otherwise this is the first round.

BACKGROUND: Commit ae5edb6 (HEAD) added a bounded repair-retry in harness/agy/adapter.go for the agy CLI failure "declaring permissions: cortex tool write_to_file: ... is not a valid artifact path; artifacts must be in ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/brain/<uuid>/". Read that commit and ephemeral/projects/tractor/agy-artifact-fix/WORK_SUMMARY.md for full context. The repair-retry is REACTIVE — it burns a failed turn before recovering. Deep research has since found a PREVENTIVE mechanism. Read both research reports (read-only, in the MAIN checkout; they will be deleted after this work, so anything durable must be distilled into your worklog deliverable):
- '/Users/tyler/src/tractor/ephemeral/deep-research-report-2.md' (primary; concrete, current as of agy CLI 1.1.15, 2026-08-19)
- '/Users/tyler/src/tractor/ephemeral/Antigravity CLI Path Configuration.md' (corroborating; note its warning that an unrecognized tool identifier in the tools allowlist makes agy HANG indefinitely)

THE MECHANISM: agy custom agents are agent.md files with YAML frontmatter supporting a `tools:` allowlist and `mainAgent: true`, selectable via `agy --agent <name>` (global: ~/.gemini/config/agents/<name>/agent.md or <name>.md; workspace-local: .agents/agents/). An agent whose tools list includes run_command and read tools but OMITS write_to_file, replace_file_content, and multi_replace_file_content structurally removes the native write tools from the model's toolset, so the artifact-path validator can never fire. The stream-json `init` event exposes `init.tools` (all available tools) for verifying the invariant.

IMPLEMENT in harness/agy:
1. Provision a Tractor-owned custom agent manifest and pass `--agent <name>` on turn invocations. Decide manifest placement (workspace-local vs global) yourself with tradeoffs documented: it must be idempotent, must not pollute pipeline workspaces in a way that shows up in git status or artifact collection (if you choose workspace-local, handle cleanup and document interaction with isolated worktree branches, which each get their own workdir), and must not clobber a user's existing agent of the same name — pick a clearly Tractor-owned name.
2. Parse the init event and enforce the invariant: if write_to_file (or the other native writers) is advertised, or run_command is absent, surface a clear terminal error naming the manifest and how to fix it. Fail fast rather than letting the model wander into the broken tool.
3. KEEP the existing repair-retry from ae5edb6 as the fallback layer — do not revert it.
4. Verify tool identifiers EMPIRICALLY, not from the reports (they disagree on names, e.g. view_file vs read_file): run bounded real agy smoke invocations — temp workspace under /tmp, model gemini-3.5-flash-low, trivial prompt, --output-format stream-json, --dangerously-skip-permissions, and ALWAYS a hard timeout (e.g. `timeout 120` or --print-timeout) because a bad tools list hangs forever. First run WITHOUT --agent to dump the canonical init.tools names; then run WITH your provisioned agent to prove write_to_file is absent and the turn completes, including a file write into the temp workspace via shell. Capture both init.tools lists as evidence. Keep total real invocations small (<= 4) and cheap.
5. Tests in the existing fake-subprocess table-driven style: --agent flag is passed; manifest provisioning is idempotent and content-correct; init.tools enforcement errors when a native writer is advertised and passes when absent; repair-retry path still works. Run `gofmt -l .` (clean), `go vet ./...`, `go test ./...` (all pass).

DELIVERABLES:
- The implementation and tests, uncommitted in the working tree.
- A worklog entry at ephemeral/worklog/202608-agy-artifact-prevention.md (use today's date 2026-08-19 in the customary timestamp prefix format — look at existing files in ephemeral/worklog/ for the naming convention). This must be a DURABLE DISTILLATION of the research since the source reports will be deleted: the failure mechanism, why no config/flag/env fixes the artifact root, the custom-agent tools allowlist mechanism with the EMPIRICALLY VERIFIED tool identifiers, the init.tools verification invariant, the PreToolUse deny-hook alternative (document it from the reports even though we are not implementing it), version constraints (pin agy 1.1.15+; hang risk with bad identifiers), the two-layer design now in Tractor (prevention + repair-retry), and the recommended upstream bug report for google-antigravity/antigravity-cli (title, reproducer, expected/actual — copy the essentials from deep-research-report-2.md's 'Upstream bug to file' section).
- WORK_SUMMARY.md in the workspace root: what you built, placement decision and tradeoffs, smoke-test evidence (both init.tools lists), test results, gofmt/vet output.

Constraints: do not modify the main checkout at /Users/tyler/src/tractor except NOTHING — treat it strictly read-only (the research files there will be deleted later by the supervisor, not you). Do not commit. Do not touch ~/.gemini beyond what manifest provisioning itself requires, and make any global write idempotent and clearly Tractor-owned.

nodes.label: Evaluate prevention (GPT)
nodes.prompt:
You are the independent adversarial validator for a change another agent just made in this workspace (a git worktree of the Tractor repo; changes uncommitted). Find real defects; do not rubber-stamp.

Context: commit ae5edb6 (HEAD) added a reactive repair-retry for the agy CLI's artifact-path turn failure ("is not a valid artifact path; artifacts must be in ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/brain/<uuid>/"). The new change adds a PREVENTION layer per deep research: a Tractor-owned agy custom agent manifest whose `tools:` allowlist omits the native write tools (write_to_file, replace_file_content, multi_replace_file_content), selected via --agent, with an init.tools invariant check, while KEEPING the repair-retry as fallback. Research sources (read-only): '/Users/tyler/src/tractor/ephemeral/deep-research-report-2.md' and '/Users/tyler/src/tractor/ephemeral/Antigravity CLI Path Configuration.md'.

VALIDATE:
1. Read WORK_SUMMARY.md, review the full diff (`git status`, `git diff`) yourself.
2. Design: is the manifest placement sound for BOTH workspace policies (shared workspace and per-branch isolated worktrees)? Idempotent? No pollution of pipeline workspaces visible to git status or artifact collection? Clearly Tractor-owned name that cannot clobber a user agent? Is --agent actually passed on turn invocations (check the args construction)? Is the repair-retry from ae5edb6 intact?
3. init.tools enforcement: does it fail fast with an actionable terminal error when a native writer is advertised or run_command is missing? Is it tolerant of unrelated tool-list changes?
4. Evidence: were tool identifiers verified EMPIRICALLY (recorded init.tools dumps in WORK_SUMMARY.md) rather than trusted from the reports (which disagree on names)? If the evidence looks fabricated or inconsistent, you may re-run ONE bounded real agy smoke test yourself (temp workspace under /tmp, model gemini-3.5-flash-low, trivial prompt, --output-format stream-json, --dangerously-skip-permissions, hard `timeout 120` guard — a bad tools list hangs forever).
5. Worklog: ephemeral/worklog/ must contain the new agy-artifact-prevention entry, and it must be a faithful, durable distillation of the research reports (compare against them directly — they will be deleted after this pipeline): failure mechanism, no-config-fix finding, allowlist mechanism with verified tool names, init.tools invariant, PreToolUse hook alternative, version constraints and hang risk, two-layer design, upstream bug recommendation. Flag any material omission or inaccuracy.
6. Run `go test ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `gofmt -l .` (expect clean) yourself.

DECIDE: if all holds, write EVAL_VERDICT.md in the workspace root (commands, outputs, judgment) and choose success. If you find material defects, write numbered actionable findings to EVAL_FEEDBACK.md (overwrite), record them in EVAL_VERDICT.md too, and route back to implement. Do not fix anything yourself. Do not commit. Treat /Users/tyler/src/tractor (main checkout) as strictly read-only.
